title: What do the Pod scheduling events report?
summary: Inspect the Pod and its events before changing requests, taints, selectors, or cluster capacity.
why: The scheduler records why no feasible node was selected.

commands.purpose: Confirm status, age, scheduler assignment, and node.

choices.label: The event is provider-specific or unclear

title: Do Pod requests exceed currently feasible allocatable resources?
summary: Compare requests, node allocatable capacity, and other scheduled workloads.
why: The scheduler uses requests, not current usage alone, when checking resource fit.

commands.purpose: Review allocatable resources and allocation summaries.

choices.label: Requests are intentional but cluster capacity is insufficient

title: Is the taint intentional and should this workload tolerate it?
summary: Compare node taints with Pod tolerations and workload policy.

choices.label: The workload is approved for those nodes
The taint correctly protects the nodes

title: Do node labels satisfy selector, affinity, and topology requirements?
summary: Compare requested placement constraints with actual labels and available topology.

choices.label: A placement rule is incorrect or obsolete
No nodes intentionally satisfy the rule

title: What is the PersistentVolumeClaim status?
summary: A Pod may remain unscheduled while a required claim is Pending or unbound.

choices.label: The claim is Pending or provisioning failed

title: Is the requested hostPort already allocated on feasible nodes?
summary: Host ports constrain placement and can prevent otherwise suitable nodes from hosting the Pod.

choices.label: The hostPort conflicts with existing workloads

title: Which quota or limit object blocks admission or scheduling?
summary: Review namespace quota and limit-range evidence before changing policy.

commands.command: kubectl describe resourcequota -n <namespace> && kubectl describe limitrange -n <namespace>

choices.label: The workload exceeds an intentional policy

title: Is a scheduler assigned and operational?
summary: No scheduling event can indicate a custom scheduler, scheduling gate, control-plane issue, or recently created Pod.

commands.purpose: Review scheduler selection and scheduling gates.

choices.label: A custom scheduler or gate is configured
Default scheduler with no clear event

title: Review workload requests before changing them
summary: Correct an accidental request only with application-owner input and non-production validation.
prerequisites: Confirm observed demand and workload SLOs.
rollback: Restore the previous manifest and rollout.

choices.label: A reviewed request correction was deployed
The request is intentional or uncertain

title: Review capacity or approved placement changes
summary: Adding capacity, changing pools, or relaxing placement affects cost and workload isolation.
prerequisites: Confirm capacity planning and cluster policy.
rollback: Use the approved node-pool or capacity rollback procedure.

title: Add only an approved toleration
summary: Do not remove protective taints or add broad tolerations without understanding isolation policy.
prerequisites: Confirm workload is permitted on tainted nodes.

title: Correct the narrow placement rule
summary: Update an obsolete selector or affinity rule only after confirming intended topology and failure-domain behavior.
prerequisites: Confirm current node labels and intended placement.

choices.label: A reviewed placement correction was deployed

title: Continue with storage evidence
summary: Preserve PVC events, StorageClass, access mode, requested capacity, and provisioner evidence. A dedicated PVC Pending journey is planned; do not treat it as available yet.

title: Review whether hostPort is necessary
summary: Changing hostPort or workload placement can affect connectivity and scheduling.
prerequisites: Confirm the service exposure design and existing port users.
rollback: Restore the previous manifest and service configuration.

title: Verify scheduling and workload readiness
summary: Confirm the Pod is scheduled and the workload becomes healthy, not merely assigned to a node.
verification: The Pod is assigned to an intended node.
Scheduling events no longer show the original failure.
Containers become Ready or provide a new, distinct diagnostic signal.
The change did not violate placement or resource policy.

choices.label: A new status such as ImagePullBackOff or CrashLoopBackOff appears

title: Recovery verified
summary: Record the scheduler evidence, actual cause, policy decision, and prevention improvement.
prevention: Review resource requests and capacity trends.
Test placement rules and storage dependencies before production rollout.
Alert on prolonged Pending and FailedScheduling events.

title: Escalate with scheduling evidence
summary: Share redacted Pod spec, scheduler name, describe events, relevant node labels/taints, resource requests, and storage status with the platform owner.
